standard.title: Development of an Asian Society in Relation to Other Nations by 1914
standard.description: the development of an Asian society in relation to other nations in the world by 1914, including the effects of ideas such as nationalism and self-determination
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can describe the development of the chosen Asian society, the effects of European contact, and the role of significant individuals and movements (AC9HH9K19–K23). They have not yet synthesised this knowledge into an account of where the chosen society stood in the world by 1914, or examined how nationalism and self-determination as ideas were reshaping Asian societies' relationships with European powers.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate the confrontation between the chosen Asian society and Western powers — such as the Sino-French war, the Russo-Japanese war, or the growing demand for Indian or Indonesian independence — explaining the effects of nationalism and self-determination on the society's development by 1914.

nodes.label: Nationalism and self-determination as ideas in the Asian context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what nationalism and self-determination meant in the context of the chosen Asian society, and describe how these ideas were taking hold by the early 20th century.
nodes.minimum_width: Students explain nationalism as the idea that a people sharing culture, language or history should govern themselves, describe how this idea was being applied in the chosen Asian society, and identify at least one movement or event that expressed it.
nodes.typical_width: Students describe how Western ideas of nationalism and self-determination — spread partly through Western education systems established under colonialism — were adopted and adapted by Asian intellectuals and movements; examine specific nationalist movements (Indian National Congress, Chinese nationalism, Indonesian nationalist organisations); explain how nationalism provided a framework for challenging colonial rule on the colonisers' own terms — using their proclaimed values against them; examine tensions within nationalist movements between moderate and radical approaches, and between different social groups' visions of the nation.
wider: Examine the paradox that Western colonialism both suppressed and enabled nationalism — by spreading ideas of rights and self-governance while denying them — and what this reveals about the internal contradictions of colonial ideology
Investigate how women participated in nationalist movements — examining the intersection of nationalism and gender politics in the chosen society
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding nationalism as an idea with a specific trajectory in the Asian context is prerequisite for understanding the confrontations and resistance movements in N2. Students who see nationalism as simply 'wanting independence' cannot explain why it emerged when it did, why it took different forms in different societies, or why it was so powerful.

response_modes.reason: Students commonly treat nationalism as self-evident — of course people want to govern themselves — without understanding it as a historically specific idea that emerged in a particular context and that required active intellectual development and political organisation to become a force. Making the idea's historical emergence explicit is the scaffold for understanding the movements of the period.

success_criteria: Explains nationalism and self-determination as ideas and describes how they applied in the chosen Asian context
Identifies at least one movement or event expressing nationalist aspiration in the chosen society

nodes.label: Confrontation and resistance — the chosen society's relationship with Western powers by 1914
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the confrontation between the chosen Asian society and Western powers, explain what the confrontation revealed about the balance of power, and assess where the society stood in relation to the world by 1914.
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe one significant confrontation between the chosen society and a Western power, explain its outcome, and describe where the society stood in relation to European powers by 1914.
nodes.typical_width: Students describe the chosen confrontation in depth — the Sino-French War (China's defeat and its effect on reform movements), the Russo-Japanese War (Japan's extraordinary victory and its global resonance), or growing Indian/Indonesian independence demands (the political mobilisation against colonial rule); explain what the confrontation revealed about the relative power of Asian societies and European powers; examine how the confrontation shaped subsequent nationalist movements and reform debates; place the chosen society's position in 1914 in the context of the whole trajectory studied — from its pre-contact features (K19) through European contact (K20) to the eve of WW1.
wider: Examine the Russo-Japanese War as a world-historical event — why did a Japanese victory over a European power resonate so strongly across Asia and what did it suggest about the future relationship between European and Asian powers?

Synthesise the whole Asian society trajectory — where did the chosen society begin (K19), what happened to it (K20–K23), and where did it stand by 1914? What does this trajectory reveal about the range of possibilities open to Asian societies facing European power?
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The synthesis task — tracing the whole trajectory from K19 to K24 — is the richest integration opportunity across the entire Asian society topic. Students who can do this well demonstrate genuine historical understanding rather than isolated factual recall. The Russo-Japanese War's global resonance is a genuinely fascinating historical question that rewards investigation.

response_modes.reason: This node draws together knowledge from K19 through K23 into a synthesis of where the chosen society stood by 1914 — coordinating political, social, economic and ideological threads developed across the whole topic.

success_criteria: Describes a significant confrontation between the chosen Asian society and a Western power and explains its outcome
Describes where the chosen society stood in relation to European powers by 1914, drawing on knowledge of the whole period studied
